usage_note: Three recommended assets comprise actual light microscopy, actual TEM, and an explicitly mixed microscopy/reconstruction figure. No AI imagery, enhancement, or synthetic data. Keep image aspect ratios and scale bars. Use contain rather than cropped cover display.

images.title: Longitudinal cardiac muscle, light microscopy, 200x
images.creator: Berkshire Community College Bioscience Image Library
images.species: Not specified in original image caption; do not identify as human solely from Commons category.
images.preparation: Longitudinal section; stain not specified in source caption.
images.scale: Source magnification 200x; no calibrated micrometer scale bar. Magnification does not reflect on-screen enlargement.
images.caption: Longitudinal light micrograph of cardiac muscle. Fine repeated striations mark sarcomeres; darker transverse intercalated discs join adjacent cardiomyocytes. Source magnification 200x; species and stain are not specified.
images.credit: Berkshire Community College Bioscience Image Library (2018), CC0, via Wikimedia Commons.

images.title: Gap junction within an intercalated disc, TEM, Figure 6
images.creator: Michael Dykstra; National Toxicology Program Rodent Ultrastructure Atlas
images.species: Rodent atlas; the figure caption does not specify an individual species.
images.preparation: Transmission electron microscopy. Atlas general methods describe aldehyde fixation, osmium postfixation, epoxy embedding, and heavy-metal-stained ultrathin sections; figure caption does not give image-specific protocol.
images.scale: Original 500 nm scale bar preserved; source magnification 49,000x.
images.license: Public domain per NTP website policy; no copyright mark appears on figure or PDF.
images.changes: Original embedded JPEG extracted losslessly with pdfimages from PDF page 7 (Figure 6); no pixel changes.
images.caption: Transmission electron micrograph of an intercalated disc. Arrow 1 identifies a gap junction, where adjacent cells form electrical coupling; arrow 2 identifies a mechanical attachment, fascia adherens. Rodent atlas; exact species not specified. Scale bar: 500 nm.
images.credit: Dykstra M. (2022), Muscle, Fig. 6. National Toxicology Program Rodent Ultrastructure Atlas. Public domain.
images.citation: Dykstra M. 2022. Muscle. In: Herbert RA, Szabo KA, Singletary E (eds.), National Toxicology Program Rodent Ultrastructure Atlas. DOI:10.22427/NTP-OTHER-1006.

images.title: Confocal images of rabbit Purkinje cells and working ventricular myocytes, Figure 2
images.creator: Daniel Romero, Oscar Camara, Frank Sachse, Rafael Sebastian
images.preparation: Fixed ventricular tissue labeled with wheat germ agglutinin (WGA)-Alexa Fluor 555, marking cell membranes and extracellular material; confocal microscopy. Published figure includes microscopy and segmentation-derived 3D reconstructions.
images.scale: Microscopy panel a:25 micrometers; panel b:30 micrometers; panel c:25 micrometers. Original scale bars retained.
images.changes: None. Publisher PNG downloaded with original panels, labels, and scale bars.
images.caption: Rabbit Purkinje cells and working ventricular myocytes. Top row: actual confocal micrographs; P identifies Purkinje cells, V a working ventricular myocyte, and PT a cell interpreted as transitional. Bottom rows: the authors’ 3D reconstructions of individual Purkinje cells, showing branched and tubular forms. WGA fluorescence highlights membranes and extracellular material.
images.limitations: Anatomical proximity alone does not prove functional electrical coupling. Authors explicitly caution that potential lateral connections seen in imaging cannot by themselves establish transmission of impulses.
images.credit: Romero D, Camara O, Sachse F, Sebastian R (2016), PLOS ONE 11:e0164093, Fig.2. CC BY 4.0. Unaltered.
images.citation: Romero D, Camara O, Sachse F, Sebastian R (2016). Analysis of Microstructure of the Cardiac Conduction System Based on Three-Dimensional Confocal Microscopy. PLOS ONE 11(10):e0164093. DOI:10.1371/journal.pone.0164093.
